clue.text: A venture lasting to all eternity, they say

indicators.note: the phrase signals that the words before are heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: for aye is an old phrase meaning for ever, lasting to all eternity

explanation.surface: Someone describes an undertaking that will go on for ever, as people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' turns FOR AYE (an old poetic way of saying for ever) into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A foray is a raid or a brief attempt at something new, so it is a venture.

clue.text: Height above sea level not attained by P.G.'s

definitions.meaning: on a ship, the height of the deck above the waterline
a P.G. is a paying guest, who never gets lodging without charge

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about an altitude that paying guests never reach.
explanation.walkthrough: P.G. is short for paying guest, a lodger who pays for room and meals; such a lodger never gets them for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval term for the vertical distance between waterline and deck; read as two words, food and lodging given without payment.

clue.text: Joey's tree-top perch

parts.note: a joey is a young kangaroo, a roo, so Joey's gives ROOS

indicators.note: the top of the word tree is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A young kangaroo sits up in the highest branches.
explanation.walkthrough: A joey is a baby kangaroo, here ROO'S; 'tree-top' gives the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a place where birds settle to rest, a perch.

clue.text: Docile bear in the middle of Hungary

parts.note: to bear fruit is to yield it

indicators.note: the central letter of the seven-letter word Hungary is taken

explanation.surface: A gentle bear found in central Hungary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' looks like the animal but is the verb, as a tree bears or yields fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone yielding gives way readily, so is docile and submissive.

clue.text: Boat made of tin going about a river

indicators.note: the container word goes around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a tin is a can
the Tamar is a river dividing Devon and Cornwall

explanation.surface: A vessel built from tinplate travels around a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar is the river between Devon and Cornwall in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a twin-hulled sailing vessel.

clue.text: Persuade business to take short cut

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: a short word has lost its tail, here the final letter

parts.note: to axe something is to cut it

explanation.surface: A firm is urged to take a shortcut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short cut' reads as a quick route, but 'short' trims the last letter from AXE, giving AX.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax is to persuade gently by flattery.

clue.text: Social occasion that ends an assembly

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are put together afresh, assembled into a new order

explanation.surface: A gathering that brings a meeting to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' rearranges THAT ENDS AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A thé dansant is a tea dance, an afternoon party with dancing.

clue.text: Prophet's patchwork

definitions.meaning: belonging to Moses, the prophet who received the Law
a picture made of small pieces set together

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for Moses, as in the Mosaic law; also art made from many small coloured tiles.

clue.text: A girl more fitted for rambling

indicators.note: the letters are fitted together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A young woman is better suited to going for country walks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fitted' rearranges A GIRL MORE; 'rambling' looks like hiking but is long-winded talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, confused account, rambling talk.

clue.text: Steel carried in container vessel

indicators.note: the answer is borne within the run of letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Metal is shipped inside a container on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steel' looks like the metal cargo but means courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel and nerve are both courage, firmness of spirit.

clue.text: Clear out of one class

parts.note: EX is Latin for out of, as in ex-directory
taken as written
a rate is a class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A pupil is let off by being taken out of a particular class.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to free someone from blame, to clear them.

clue.text: Tease American about sweetheart

indicators.note: turned about, the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: Someone teases an American about the person they love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns RAGUS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar is an affectionate form of address for a loved one.

clue.text: Happen to be before time

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second in the answer

parts.note: taken as written
tide is an old word for time or season, as in Yuletide

explanation.surface: Someone is told to arrive early.
explanation.walkthrough: TIDE as time survives in Yuletide and Eastertide.
explanation.definitionFit: To betide someone is to befall them, as in woe betide you.

clue.text: Fencing with a friend is a duel without seconds

parts.note: a pal is a friend
taken as written

indicators.note: the second and fourth letters of duel are dropped, keeping the odd ones

explanation.surface: A fencing bout between pals, fought without anyone acting as second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fencing' and 'duel' suggest swordplay; seconds are a duellist's assistants, but here they are the even letters of DUEL, leaving DE.
explanation.definitionFit: A palisade is a fence of pointed stakes, fencing round an area.

clue.text: Wool owner is a disgrace to his family

definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme, the dark animal asked whether it has any wool
the member of a family who brings it shame

explanation.definitionFit: In 'Baa baa' the animal with three bags full; and the idiom for a family's disreputable member.

clue.text: Little Tich's cobbler must have worked here finally

definitions.text: Little Tich's cobbler must have worked here
definitions.meaning: Little Tich, a music hall comic, danced in huge boots, so his bootmaker needed a lengthy foot-shaped mould

explanation.walkthrough: Little Tich was a short British music hall comedian famous for his dance in boots over two feet long; a cobbler shapes boots on a last.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler's mould for very big boots; and the phrase for something that comes after a long delay.

clue.text: By turning up in the city precincts layabout is identified

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, often just called the city in crosswords

indicators.note: the turned piece sits inside the city and precincts

parts.note: zones are districts or precincts

indicators.note: in a down answer the word by is turned upwards, read backwards

explanation.surface: An idler is spotted after showing up in the city centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses BY to YB, which goes into LA + ZONES.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazybones is a lazy person, an idler.

clue.text: Stick up letters after work

definitions.meaning: to display a notice on a board
the Latin prefix meaning later, as in postwar

explanation.surface: A notice is put up about mail arriving after the working day.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up a notice; mail; the Latin word for later; and a job, as in a vacancy.

clue.text: Let assets get squandered without discernment

indicators.note: letters thrown about wastefully are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Wasting money shows poor judgment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get squandered' rearranges LET ASSETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasteless means lacking good taste, showing no discernment.

clue.text: A spell of Merlin's beginning to trouble troubadour

indicators.note: the wizard's magic transforms the letters into a new arrangement
the opening letter of trouble is taken

explanation.surface: Merlin casts a spell that spells trouble for a wandering singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A spell of' rearranges MERLINS plus T, from 'beginning to trouble'.
explanation.definitionFit: A minstrel is a medieval travelling singer, like a troubadour.

clue.text: You can hear rabbits sleep

indicators.note: the words signal that the word is listened to, not read

parts.note: female rabbits are called does

explanation.surface: Rabbits can be heard sleeping.
explanation.walkthrough: A doe is a female rabbit; DOES said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To doze is to sleep lightly, nap.

clue.text: Deficiency — various instances start to surface

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of instances arranged in different ways
the opening letter of surface is taken

explanation.surface: Shortcomings start to show in a number of cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges INSTANCES to SCANTINES, then S from 'start to surface'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scantiness is meagreness, a lack or insufficiency.

clue.text: Will appeals to umpire finally

parts.note: pleas are appeals

indicators.note: the last letter of umpire is taken

explanation.surface: Cricketers keep appealing to the umpire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' is the verb, as in 'do as you will'.
explanation.definitionFit: To please is to wish or choose, as in do as you please.

clue.text: Rally is held in port in Alabama

indicators.note: the short word is held inside the name of the port

parts.note: Mobile is a port city in Alabama

explanation.surface: A rally takes place in an Alabama port.
explanation.definitionFit: To mobilise supporters is to rally them for action.

clue.text: Bicycle was blue

explanation.definitionFit: A low-powered cycle with an engine; and the past tense of a verb for feeling gloomy.

clue.text: Property of French art gallery

parts.note: in French, tu es means thou art
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: A building owned by a French art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is the old form of 'are': French 'tu es' is 'thou art'. The Tate is a group of British art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is land or possessions, one's property.

clue.text: An easterner, like Mr Fleming

parts.note: as means like
Ian Fleming wrote the James Bond novels

explanation.surface: A person from the east resembles a well-known author.
explanation.definitionFit: An Asian is a person from Asia, in the east.

clue.text: Knocks up box here

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word is read backwards from the bottom

parts.note: raps are knocks

explanation.surface: Someone knocks up a box here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocks up' looks like a phrasal verb; 'up' reverses RAPS. 'box' is the verb, to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box in practice.

clue.text: Bearlike creature originating in 12

annotationWithheld.why: Bearlike creature originating in 12: the wordplay reads the first two letters of 12 (PALISADE) as 'P and A'; no 'and' is in the clue, and neither rebus nor reverse forms are accepted for it

clue.text: Know-how can make tax bold instead of conservative

indicators.note: one piece replaces the other within the tax word

parts.note: excise is a tax on goods
pert means bold or cheeky

explanation.surface: Skill can make a tax stand out rather than stay modest.
explanation.walkthrough: In EXCISE the C is replaced by PERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Expertise is special skill, practical know-how.

clue.text: The lady's got a beautiful valley, with a river, to paint

parts.note: Di is a crossword name for a lady, so the lady's is DIS
the Vale of Tempe is a famous scenic valley in Greece
R is short for river

explanation.surface: A woman paints a lovely valley and its river.
explanation.walkthrough: Tempe is a beautiful valley in Thessaly, celebrated by classical poets.
explanation.definitionFit: Distemper is a water-based paint; as a verb it means to paint with it.

clue.text: German left the course

explanation.definitionFit: German for the opposite of rechts; and the British term for a golf course by the sea.
